topic: Why small choices feel completely exhausting after a long day

script.title: Decision Fatigue Explained: Why Simple Choices Feel Exhausting
script.hook: Why does picking a simple movie feel totally exhausting?

scenes.text: Why does picking a simple movie feel totally exhausting?
You make about thirty five thousand decisions every single day.
Every micro choice drains the exact same mental fuel tank.
Psychologists call this phenomenon decision fatigue.
By five o clock, your willpower is fundamentally depleted.
So your brain seeks an easy shortcut to survive.

motion_action.query_text: why is making choices hard at night
motion_action.result_headline: The brain avoids complex trade-offs when tired

scenes.text: It either chooses nothing or picks the default option.
That is why scrolling Netflix for an hour feels easier than watching.

motion_action.result_headline: Status quo bias during mental exhaustion

scenes.text: To fight this, automate routine choices before your day begins.
